kiribati_tabakea.name: Turn his own shell into the land of Banaba
kiribati_tabakea.notes: In the Banaban (Ocean Island) cosmogony the primordial turtle Tabakea is the first of all beings, and the island of Banaba is formed from his carapace; he is the giant turtle upon whose back the land rests.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions: Writings on the Atoll Culture of the Gilbert Islands

kiribati_tabakea.name: Bring forth Nareau from a clam shell
kiribati_tabakea.notes: In the Banaban recension Tabakea burns a small lizard, sets the ashes in a clam shell of water, and after three moons the demiurge Nareau emerges as a tiny dark man whom Tabakea claims as son.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions; Banaban creation account

kiribati_te_ikawai.name: Stand as the first-born of the second generation
kiribati_te_ikawai.notes: Te Ikawai (the Eldest) is named in the Tungaru creation-genealogy as the senior child of the generation that springs from Na Atibu, heading the line of personified primordial beings.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions, creation genealogy

kiribati_te_nao.name: Embody the surge of the sea-wave
kiribati_te_nao.notes: Te Nao (the Wave) is the personified ocean-swell, one of the named second-generation beings of the Tungaru creation-genealogy who arise as Nareau orders the primal darkness.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions, creation genealogy

kiwai_dirivo.name: Dwell as mistress in the land of the dead
kiwai_dirivo.notes: Daughter of the eponymous Adiri and bride of Sido, she receives the first man to die into the underworld of Adiri in Landtman's recension of the Kiwai death-myth.

sources.reference: G. Landtman, The Folk-Tales of the Kiwai Papuans; The Kiwai Papuans of British New Guinea

kiwai_nuga.name: Take the shape of a crocodile-man
kiwai_nuga.notes: A theriomorphic origin-ancestor born from wood, Nuga is a crocodile-man whose form joins human and crocodile, one of the renowned Kiwai mythic figures alongside Sido and Marunogere.

sources.reference: G. Landtman, The Kiwai Papuans of British New Guinea

kongo_simbi.name: Appear as snake, fire-spark, vine or human
kongo_simbi.notes: The bisimbi nature-spirits manifest in many forms - a person, a great serpent, a calabash vine, pottery, or a spark of fire (kalunga) like the spark that began the world.

sources.reference: W. MacGaffey, Religion and Society in Central Africa: The BaKongo of Lower Zaire

kongo_simbi.name: Travel the kalunga line between the living and the dead
kongo_simbi.notes: Bisimbi are intermediaries who cross the kalunga boundary between Ku Seke (the world of the living) and Ku Mpemba (the world of the ancestors), guiding souls and linking the living to the dead.

sources.reference: W. MacGaffey, Religion and Society in Central Africa

korean_cheonjiwang.name: Descend and sire the star-king twins
korean_cheonjiwang.notes: After ordering heaven and earth the celestial king Cheonjiwang descends and lies with the earthly woman Chongmyong-buin (Baji-wang), begetting the twin sons Daebyeolwang and Sobyeolwang.

sources.reference: Cheonjiwang Bonpuri (Jeju creation hymn), as recorded in Korean shamanic narrative collections

korean_cheonjiwang.name: Decree the destruction of the doubled sun and moon
korean_cheonjiwang.notes: He instructs his sons to shoot down the surplus sun and surplus moon with bows of melted iron, making the scorched and frozen world fit to live in.

sources.reference: Cheonjiwang Bonpuri (Jeju creation hymn)

korean_daebyeolwang.name: Grow the true flower in the contest for the worlds
korean_daebyeolwang.notes: In the flower-growing contest for rule of the living world the honest elder twin grows the genuine bloom, but his brother swaps the pots in his sleep and steals the living world by fraud, so Daebyeolwang takes the realm of the dead.

sources.reference: Cheonjiwang Bonpuri (Jeju creation hymn)

korean_habaek.name: Contend in a shapeshifting duel
korean_habaek.notes: Outraged at Haemosu's abduction of his daughter Yuhwa, the river-god turns into a carp, a deer, and a quail in a metamorphosis contest, but is bested at each turn (otter, wolf, hawk).

sources.reference: Yi Gyu-bo, Dongmyeongwang-pyeon; Samguk Yusa

korean_sobyeolwang.name: Win the living world by the swapped flower
korean_sobyeolwang.notes: The younger star-king twin steals rule of the living world by switching the contest-flowers while his elder brother sleeps, so that the world of the living falls under his flawed and deceitful order.

sources.reference: Cheonjiwang Bonpuri (Jeju creation hymn)

korean_yuri.name: Prove his descent with the broken sword
korean_yuri.notes: Yuri recovers the missing half of Jumong's broken sword, hidden under a pillar, and presents it at Jolbon to be recognized as the founder's true son and heir to Goguryeo.

sources.reference: Samguk Sagi, Goguryeo annals, reign of Yuri

korean_yuri.name: Compose the Song of the Orioles (Hwangjoga)
korean_yuri.notes: Grieving over the strife between his wives Chihui and Hwahui and watching a pair of orioles, King Yuri sings the Hwangjoga, the oldest recorded Korean lyric, lamenting his solitude.

sources.reference: Samguk Sagi, Goguryeo annals, third year of Yuri (Hwangjoga)

koryak_yiniaaneut.name: Recover the sun swallowed by Raven
koryak_yiniaaneut.notes: Daughter of Big-Raven, she frees the captured sun in the best-known Koryak light-origin tale, a Kamchatkan parallel to the North Pacific Coast sun-release myths.

sources.reference: W. Jochelson, The Koryak (Jesup North Pacific Expedition)

krachi_dente.name: Pronounce oracles consulted in matters of war
krachi_dente.notes: From the cave-shrine at Kete-Krachi on the Volta, Dente delivered oracles sought across the region; the Asante state consulted him in matters of war and statecraft, making his shrine a pan-regional pilgrimage centre.

sources.reference: A. W. Cardinall, Tales Told in Togoland; D. Maier, Priests and Power: The Case of the Dente Shrine

kuba_mweel.name: Become ancestral mother of the Kuba lineages
kuba_mweel.notes: Sister-wife of Woot, Mweel is the ancestral mother from whom the Kuba lineages descend; her union with her brother Woot founds the line of the Children of Woot.

sources.reference: E. Torday & T. A. Joyce, Notes ethnographiques sur les peuples communement appeles Bakuba

kwakwakawakw_bakwas.name: Dig ghost-cockles on lonely beaches
kwakwakawakw_bakwas.notes: The wild man of the woods leaves the forest for isolated beaches to dig dzoli (cockles), his favoured ghost-food, earning him the name Cockle Hunter.

sources.reference: F. Boas, The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians; Kwakwaka'wakw oral tradition

kwakwakawakw_komokwa.name: Command the seals and sea-mammals
kwakwakawakw_komokwa.notes: Chief of the undersea world, he is master and protector of seals and sea-lions; the posts and beams of his copper house are living sea-lions, and killer whales, loons and sculpins attend him.

sources.reference: F. Boas, Kwakiutl Tales; Kwakwaka'wakw oral tradition of the undersea chief

kwakwakawakw_komokwa.name: Bestow the wealth cast up by the sea
kwakwakawakw_komokwa.notes: As the Wealthy One and Copper Maker he governs the riches deposited on shore by the tides, the storms of winter and the calm of summer, and can heal and grant supernatural gifts to those he favours.

sources.reference: F. Boas, Kwakiutl Tales; G. Hunt field materials

kuba_woot.gloss: the first man and first king

sources.reference: E. Torday & T. A. Joyce, Notes ethnographiques sur les Bakuba

kiribati_tabuariki.name: Invocation of the thunder-anti
kiribati_tabuariki.notes: Tabuariki was the most prominent of the anti invoked by the Tungaru; as a healer who ruled the winds and rain he was called upon for health and for relief from storm and drought.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions

kiwai_marunogere.name: The moguru fertility rite
kiwai_marunogere.notes: Marunogere is the culture-hero who instituted the moguru, the great Kiwai fertility rite of communal license and initiation in which ancestral effigies are displayed in the longhouse; the rite descends from his founding act.

sources.reference: G. Landtman, The Kiwai Papuans of British New Guinea (moguru rite)

krachi_dente.name: The Dente cave-oracle at Kete-Krachi
krachi_dente.notes: One of the oldest shrine institutions of the region, the Dente cave-oracle on the Volta drew pilgrims and state envoys; its priest spoke for the god, and the shrine prohibited bloodshed and dispensed social justice.

sources.reference: D. Maier, Priests and Power: The Case of the Dente Shrine

korean_tangun.name: Veneration of Dangun as national progenitor and mountain-god
korean_tangun.notes: After his reign Dangun is said to have become the mountain-spirit (sansin) of Asadal; he is venerated as the progenitor of the Korean nation, with later Daejonggyo worship and the Gaecheonjeol observance.

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

korean_habaek.name: Worship by the Goguryeo royal house
korean_habaek.notes: As maternal grandfather of the founder Jumong, the river-god Habaek was honoured by the Goguryeo kings in their dynastic cult of divine descent.

sources.reference: Gwanggaeto Stele; Yi Gyu-bo, Dongmyeongwang-pyeon

kongo_simbi.name: Veneration of the bisimbi at springs and pools
kongo_simbi.notes: Local bisimbi inhabiting rocks, gullies, streams and pools were venerated as guardians of fertility and well-being; banganga sought their guidance, and their power was bound into minkisi (sacred charms).

sources.reference: W. MacGaffey, Religion and Society in Central Africa

kwakwakawakw_dzunukwa.name: The masked Dzunukwa dance in the winter ceremonial
kwakwakawakw_dzunukwa.notes: Dzunukwa is danced in the winter potlatch ceremonial; as one of the three foremost crests (with Thunderbird and Sisiutl) she is displayed in mask-dances and her image legitimates chiefly wealth and prerogative.

sources.reference: F. Boas, The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians

kwakwakawakw_bakwas.name: The Bukwus mask-dance
kwakwakawakw_bakwas.notes: The wild man of the woods is impersonated in the winter T'seka and Tla'sala dances, the masked performer holding a forearm before the face to mime the spirit's shyness of humankind.

sources.reference: F. Boas, The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians

sacredAnimals.name: Sea turtle
sacredAnimals.notes: Tabakea is himself the primordial turtle on whose back the land rests; the turtle is his very form.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions

sacredAnimals.name: Eel
sacredAnimals.notes: Riiki is the monstrous sky-lifting eel of the Tungaru cosmogony, his elongated form mirrored in the band of the Milky Way into which he is set.

sources.reference: A. Grimble, Tungaru Traditions

attributes.name: Birth from an egg
attributes.notes: Conceived when sunlight followed Yuhwa, Jumong is born from a large egg that animals refuse to harm and that warms in the sun until the boy hatches.

sources.reference: Samguk Sagi; Yi Gyu-bo, Dongmyeongwang-pyeon

sacredAnimals.name: Fish and turtles of the river
sacredAnimals.notes: Fleeing pursuit, Jumong strikes the water and fish and turtles rise to form a bridge that carries him across, then disperse behind him.

sources.reference: Samguk Sagi, Goguryeo annals

attributes.name: Chariot drawn by five dragons
attributes.notes: Haemosu descends from heaven in a chariot pulled by five dragons (oryonggeo), his retinue riding swans, when he founds Bukbuyeo.

sources.reference: Yi Gyu-bo, Dongmyeongwang-pyeon

sacredPlants.name: Sacred sandalwood tree (Sindansu)
sacredPlants.notes: Dangun is born of the union beneath the sacred Sindansu (sandalwood/birch) tree where Hwanung descended; his name Dangun is read as 'Sandalwood Ruler.'

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

attributes.name: The Three Heavenly Seals (Cheonbuin)
attributes.notes: Hwanin bestows on Hwanung the three heavenly seals - a bronze mirror, bronze bell and bronze dagger - tokens of heavenly authority for his descent to rule mankind.

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

attributes.name: Descent to the sacred tree with 3,000 followers
attributes.notes: Hwanung descends to the peak of Mt. Taebaek at the sandalwood tree (Sindansu) with the three seals and 3,000 followers, founding the 'divine city' (sinsi) and the wind, rain and cloud spirits.

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

sacredPlants.name: Mugwort and garlic
sacredPlants.notes: The bear becomes the woman Ungnyeo by enduring 100 days in a cave on nothing but a bundle of sacred mugwort (ssuk) and twenty cloves of garlic, per Hwanung's instruction.

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

sacredAnimals.name: Bear
sacredAnimals.notes: Ungnyeo ('Bear-Woman') is originally a she-bear who alone completes the cave-trial that the tiger abandons.

sources.reference: Iryeon, Samguk Yusa, Gojoseon

sacredPlants.name: The five grains
sacredPlants.notes: Jacheongbi brings the seeds of the five grains (ogok) down from heaven to humanity, the founding gift of farming in the Segyeong Bonpuri.

sources.reference: Segyeong Bonpuri (Jeju agricultural hymn)

sacredPlants.name: Flower of resurrection
sacredPlants.notes: She wins from the Seocheon flower-field the herb/flower of life with which she revives the dead.

sources.reference: Segyeong Bonpuri (Jeju agricultural hymn)

attributes.name: Donned and doffed raven shape
attributes.notes: Big-Raven puts on and takes off his raven coat at will, moving between bird and human form as the first man and great shaman.

sources.reference: W. Jochelson, The Koryak

sacredAnimals.name: Raven
sacredAnimals.notes: The raven is his defining form and namesake (Kutkynnaku), the creator-trickster of the Kamchatkan peoples.

sources.reference: W. Jochelson, The Koryak

attributes.name: The white giant who vomits creation
attributes.notes: Mbombo is pictured as an immense white giant who, in stomach-pain, vomits forth the sun, moon, stars, the nine animals and the first peoples upon the primal water.

sources.reference: E. Torday & T. A. Joyce, Notes ethnographiques sur les Bakuba

attributes.name: Black pursed-lip mask and the cry 'hu, hu'
attributes.notes: Dzunukwa is shown in a dark mask with sunken eyes and a rounded, pursed mouth uttering her booming 'hu, hu'; carried on her back is the burden-basket in which she bears off children.

sources.reference: F. Boas, The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians

attributes.name: Green hooked-nose mask with skull-like face
attributes.notes: Bakwas is masked as a gaunt green being with a skeletal face, sunken eyes, hooked beak-like nose and hemlock-bark rings, a wild man half the height of a person.

sources.reference: F. Boas, The Social Organization and the Secret Societies of the Kwakiutl Indians

sacredAnimals.name: Cockle
sacredAnimals.notes: The cockle (dzoli) he digs and offers as ghost-food is his emblematic creature.

sources.reference: Kwakwaka'wakw oral tradition

attributes.name: Sea-creature mask and ceremonial copper
attributes.notes: Komokwa is masked as a fusion of sea-mammal and undersea beings, hung with abalone and copper, ruling from a copper house guarded by sea-lion posts.

sources.reference: F. Boas, Kwakiutl Tales

sacredAnimals.name: Killer whale and seal
sacredAnimals.notes: Killer whales, seals, sea-lions, loons and sculpins are his attendant creatures.

sources.reference: F. Boas, Kwakiutl Tales
